info.title: CF Meet public API
info.description: Aggregate customer-facing API reference of the CF Meet public API Gateway, generated from the authoritative service contracts and the explicit public route allow-list. Each service keeps its own API version (x-cfmeet-source-version); there is no monolithic version. Internal, operator and provider-callback operations are never included.

post.summary: Register an application endpoint of a principal
post.description: Requires calls.write. The principal is resolved inside the credential's scope (unknown, foreign or inactive: 404). Registering the same endpointKey again for the same principal refreshes the endpoint (200); a key held by another principal is 409.

get.description: Requires calls.read. Only endpoints of the credential's scope; a foreign principal has none.

delete.description: Requires calls.write. The endpoint is never rung again; its live offers are cancelled and its signaling credentials stop working. Revoking a revoked endpoint is a no-op.

get.description: Signaling credential. Recovery after a reconnect: the canonical call history of the credential's principal (every device of it sees the same entries), with the same derivation and filters as GET /v1/calls?principalId= — a client that missed every push and realtime signal reads the authoritative missed / answered outcome here. principalId is not accepted (an endpoint reads its own principal only).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): INBOUND (the principal was a recipient) or OUTBOUND (the principal initiated the Call).

parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): the participant outcome derived from Call evidence.

parameters.name: missed
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): true lists only Calls the principal missed (outcome MISSED); false excludes them.

parameters.name: enterpriseDestinationType
parameters.description: With enterpriseDestinationId: only Calls routed through this enterprise destination (an extension — as dialed or reached —, a ring group, a queue, an IVR flow or a voicemail mailbox of the same scope). Never a public contact.

200.description: One page of the principal's history.

get.description: Signaling credential. The endpoint's live and recently finished offers with the authoritative Call state; only unexpired RINGING offers of answerable calls are actionable. Stale client state is never trusted.

post.summary: Accept one's own ring offer
post.description: Signaling credential: only an offer addressed to the credential's own endpoint (any other offer is 404). Same arbitration and semantics as POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/accept.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Decline one's own ring offer
post.description: Signaling credential: only an offer addressed to the credential's own endpoint (any other offer is 404). Same arbitration and semantics as POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/decline.

get.summary: Open the endpoint's realtime signaling channel (WebSocket)
get.description: Authenticated before the upgrade with the endpoint's signaling credential. Delivery only: the server sends signaling.ready, then the endpoint's realtime signals (cfmeet.calling.realtime-signal, https://schemas.cfmeet.com/calling/realtime/v1.schema.json), answers {"type":"ping"} with signaling.pong and closes with code 4001 when the credential expires. Signals are sent only after the authoritative transaction committed; a lost signal never loses state (recover with GET /v1/calling/invitations and the call API). Commands use HTTP.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the WebSocket channel is open (subprotocol cfmeet.signaling.v1 when it was offered).

post.summary: Mint a signaling credential for one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Called by the application backend, which hands the short-lived credential to the device. The device never receives the platform API credential.

201.description: The signaling credential (secret: deliver it to the device only).

get.summary: List the caller's calls, or one principal's call history (newest first, keyset pagination)
get.description: Requires the calls.read scope. Ordered by createdAt descending, then callId descending. Only the bounded filters below are accepted; unknown or repeated query parameters are rejected with 400. The cursor is opaque, carries position only and never scope. Part F §62: with principalId the response is that principal's canonical call history (CallHistoryList): only Calls it participates in, each with its participant-relative direction and outcome derived from Call evidence (never from push or realtime delivery), safe enterprise labels, the voicemail link for mailbox owners and recording availability; direction / outcome / missed need principalId. enterpriseDestinationType + enterpriseDestinationId narrow either listing.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque nextCursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: principalId
parameters.description: Part F §62: this principal's history (a principal of the credential's scope; any other id yields an empty page).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): INBOUND (the principal was a recipient) or OUTBOUND (the principal initiated the Call).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): the participant outcome derived from Call evidence.

parameters.name: missed
parameters.description: History only (needs a principal): true lists only Calls the principal missed (outcome MISSED); false excludes them.

parameters.name: enterpriseDestinationType
parameters.description: With enterpriseDestinationId: only Calls routed through this enterprise destination (an extension — as dialed or reached —, a ring group, a queue, an IVR flow or a voicemail mailbox of the same scope). Never a public contact.

200.description: One page of calls (CallList), or with principalId one page of history (CallHistoryList).

post.summary: Create and ring an application call
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. Creates the Call (REQUESTED), records the APP_DIRECT_V1 authorization, resolves the target principals inside the credential's scope, selects the APPLICATION route, prepares the Call's media resource through the configured media provider, authorizes the initiator's session and rings every eligible endpoint of every target (one offer each, server-owned expiry). Answers 201 with the call (normally RINGING). A replay with the same key returns the recorded response; the call is never created twice.

201.description: The call was created (or the recorded response of an identical earlier request).

get.summary: Get one call with its participants, sessions and durations
get.description: Requires the calls.read scope. A call that does not exist, belongs to another tenant, application or environment, or whose id is malformed is answered with the same 404.

post.summary: Report an unwanted or abusive call
post.description: Part H §69: a participant principal of the call reports it with a bounded category and optional code (no free text, no number). Idempotent per reporter and call.

post.summary: Accept a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Exactly one device per participant wins (single-winner arbitration in the database); the participant's other offers become ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE and lose every media path. The first winning participant moves the Call to ANSWERED. An expired offer is 410; an offer that is no longer live (cancelled, answered elsewhere, declined) is 409.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

get.summary: Actions currently available on a call
get.description: Requires calls.read. Server-derived from the Call's state, its live offers, the credential's scopes and the media provider's capabilities.

post.summary: Cancel a call before it is active
post.description: Requires calls.write. Pre-active termination (REQUESTED ... ANSWERED): cancels live offers and outstanding attempts, closes route, leg and sessions and tears down the media resource. Repeating it on a CANCELLED call is a no-op.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Decline a ring offer on behalf of one endpoint
post.description: Requires calls.write. Declines only this endpoint's offer; other devices keep ringing. The Call ends as DECLINED only when every live offer of every pending target is declined.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: End an active call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Moves the Call to ENDING, removes every media connection and terminates the media resource; the Call becomes ENDED only on cleanup evidence (otherwise it stays ENDING and the reconciler retries). Usage and quality are finalized.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Hold a connected call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Enforced at the media provider: every admitted connection loses audio and video publishing (subscription unchanged) before the Call becomes HELD. A provider that cannot update permissions is 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE; an unconfirmed update is 503 MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE and the Call stays CONNECTED.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Send one key to the IVR (RTC caller)
post.description: Part F section 57. Requires calls.write and enterprise.calls.use. Only the Call's initiator endpoint may press keys (another endpoint or scope: 404). The key is used once and never stored or logged. accepted=false when the Call does not wait for a key (stale input is ignored).

200.description: Whether the IVR took the key.

get.description: Requires enterprise.recording.read; a participant or a recording administrator.

parameters.name: principalId
parameters.description: Act for this principal, who must be a participant of the Call (else 404). Without it the credential must hold enterprise.recording.manage and acts as a recording administrator.

post.summary: Record a participant's recording consent
post.description: Requires calls.write and enterprise.calls.use. The participant's OWN decision through its endpoint; idempotent on replay.

post.summary: Start recording a Call
post.description: Requires enterprise.recording.manage. Creates an immutable recording authorization first (kill switch CALL_RECORDING_ENABLED, enterprise Call, ACTIVE default policy and mode, CONNECTED, actor, server-issued notice, each required participant's own consent, protected storage, a capture path). ALLOWED: 201 with the recording; a Call already being recorded: 200 with it (idempotent); DENIED: 403 RECORDING_NOT_AUTHORIZED (the decision and reason are in recording-authorizations).

get.description: Requires enterprise.recording.read; a participant (principalId) or a recording administrator.

parameters.name: principalId
parameters.description: Act for this principal, who must be a participant of the Call (else 404). Without it the credential must hold enterprise.recording.manage and acts as a recording administrator.

post.summary: Stop a recording
post.description: Requires enterprise.recording.manage; a participant or a recording administrator. STOPPING (EXPLICIT); the capture is then finalized into protected storage. Never blocked by a kill switch. Audited.

parameters.name: recording_id
parameters.description: Recording id (another scope's, or a Call the principal was not part of, is 404).

post.summary: Resume a held call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Re-derives every connection's permissions from the currently authorized server state (never from a stored pre-hold grant) and applies them at the provider before the Call becomes CONNECTED.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Issue a media credential for a session
post.description: Requires calls.write. Issues a short-lived join credential for one session whose media access the server authorized (the initiator's session, or a participant's single winning device) while the Call is in a media state. Capabilities derive from server state only; the body must be empty. A losing, removed or ended session, or a terminal Call, is 409.

post.summary: Remove one session from a call
post.description: Requires calls.write. Ends the session and revokes its media access for ever: its credentials stop working, the provider connection is removed (or queued for enforcement) and any re-entry is evicted. The Call's state is not changed; removing a removed session again is a no-op.

200.description: The session was removed (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Transfer a participant's place to another principal
post.description: Requires calls.write and an Idempotency-Key. The same Call continues (TRANSFERRING): the target's endpoints are rung with TRANSFER offers; when the target joins with a media path the transferring participant is retired and the Call returns to CONNECTED. If the target declines, does not answer or cannot join, the transfer FAILS and the Call returns to its pre-transfer state (CONNECTED or HELD) when the remaining parties still have a media path.

200.description: The command's result (or the recorded response of an identical earlier command).

post.summary: Create a communication context
post.description: Creates a Communication Context (version 1): the consumer-neutral authority for WHY (opaque externalContextReference), WHO (participants: principal ids or opaque ContactReference ids), in which DIRECTION, over which CHANNEL, during which window and under which bounded policy parties may communicate. Requires privacy.contexts.write and an Idempotency-Key. Referenced principals must be active principals of the credential's own application environment. Scope comes only from the credential; status, version, authorization results, telephone numbers, providers and relay numbers are never inputs. One context per external reference in an application environment. 503 PRIVACY_RELAY_DISABLED while the feature is disabled.

201.description: The created context (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

get.description: Contexts of the credential's application environment, newest first, keyset-paginated (no offsets). Requires privacy.contexts.read.
Requires privacy.contexts.read. A context of another tenant, application or environment is answered exactly like a missing one (404 CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND).

patch.description: Typed, versioned configuration update (participant replacement / reassignment on the SAME context, channels, directions, validity, bounded policy, allowed strategies) — never a status patch or an arbitrary merge patch. Requires privacy.contexts.write, expectedVersion (409 CONTEXT_VERSION_CONFLICT when stale; a stale write can never restore removed authority) and an Idempotency-Key. The version increments exactly once; removed participants lose authority the moment the update commits, in every relay session; active calls of removed participants are terminated when the policy says so (enforcement.status APPLIED or PENDING, never claimed early).

post.summary: Complete a context
post.description: Explicit lifecycle command (no status patch). Requires privacy.contexts.write, expectedVersion and an Idempotency-Key. -> COMPLETED (never back to ACTIVE): relay sessions complete; new calls during the grace period only when graceAllowsNewCalls; without remaining grace active calls are terminated; after the final grace all authority ends.

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

get.description: Lifecycle, versions, participant and direction history, sessions, recent authorization decisions, audit events and enforcement status for support and debugging. Never contact values. Requires privacy.contexts.read.

post.summary: Resume a context
post.description: Explicit lifecycle command (no status patch). Requires privacy.contexts.write, expectedVersion and an Idempotency-Key. SUSPENDED -> ACTIVE, only while the validity window remains and never from COMPLETED, REVOKED or EXPIRED.

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

post.summary: Revoke a context
post.description: Explicit lifecycle command (no status patch). Requires privacy.contexts.write, expectedVersion and an Idempotency-Key. -> REVOKED (terminal, irreversible): every relay session is revoked, all new authority is denied, active calls are terminated when terminateActiveCallsOnRevoke. Repeating it is a safe idempotent answer.

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

post.summary: Create a Privacy Relay Session
post.description: Creates a Privacy Relay Session (NOT a call: one session may authorize many call attempts during its window) under a relay strategy. Requires privacy.sessions.write and an Idempotency-Key. Participants, channels, directions, validity and strategy may only NARROW the context; anything broader is refused (PARTICIPANT_NOT_AUTHORIZED, CHANNEL_NOT_ALLOWED, DIRECTION_NOT_ALLOWED, STRATEGY_NOT_ALLOWED, VALIDITY_NOT_CONTAINED). Strategies are policy: only the application route is executable today.

post.summary: Suspend a context
post.description: Explicit lifecycle command (no status patch). Requires privacy.contexts.write, expectedVersion and an Idempotency-Key. ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED: new authority is denied immediately; active calls are terminated when terminateActiveCallsOnSuspend.

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

get.description: Sessions of the credential's application environment, newest first, keyset-paginated. Requires privacy.sessions.read.

get.summary: Privacy-safe call evidence of a Relay Session
get.description: Requires privacy.evidence.read (knowing a session id is never enough). Calling verifies with Privacy Relay, in the credential's scope, that the session exists for the caller — a session of another scope is exactly 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND — then returns evidence from its OWN Call records: canonical timestamps, final state, normalized terminal reason and failure category, Calling's authoritative connected duration (never requestedAt -> endedAt), per-participant connected time, attempts, route class and the Privacy Relay decision ids. NO_ANSWER comes from the canonical Call record (independent of push delivery). Never a telephone number, masked number, Contact Vault material, provider / carrier identifier, provider payload or credential. Keyset pages (limit 1-100, default 25); 503 when ownership cannot be proven.

post.summary: Resume a session

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

post.summary: Revoke a session

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

post.summary: Suspend a session

200.description: The command result (or the recorded result of an identical earlier request).

calling.Call.description: One call with participants, session summaries and durations. Durations of open connections are measured up to durationsAsOf (the call's end for terminal calls). connectedDurationMs runs from the first CONNECTED to the end (null if never connected). invitations are the Call's ring offers (one per target endpoint and ring round); transfers its application transfers.

calling.CallCounterpart.description: Another participant of the Call (internal display identity only).

calling.CallHistoryEnterprise.description: Safe enterprise labels of an enterprise Call: the dialed internal extension (a short code or alias, never a telephone number), its label, the routing phase / outcome and the current ring group / queue labels.

calling.CallHistoryEntry.description: A Call as it appears in one principal's history.

durationMs.description: From CONNECTED to the end of the Call; null while it lasts or if it never connected.

recordingAvailable.description: A READY call recording exists (metadata and audio through the authorized, audited recording routes).

calling.CallHistoryList.description: One page of a principal's call history, newest Call first (createdAt DESC, callId DESC).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

calling.CallHistoryVoicemail.description: The voicemail message left on the Call — present only for an owner of its mailbox. Its audio is reached through the authorized, audited voicemail routes (never a URL here).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

calling.CallParticipant.description: A logical participant. displayName is presentation metadata only and never identifies anyone. connectedDurationMs is the union of the participant's session connection intervals (concurrent devices are not double counted).

calling.CallParticipation.description: The principal's own part in the Call (one per logical participant, whatever its devices).

answeredAt.description: When the participant (any device) answered; for the initiator, when the Call was answered.

calling.CallSession.description: Summary of one device / network participation of a participant (its media / signaling identity is not exposed). connectionCount is the number of connection intervals opened (1 + reconnects). endpointId is the application endpoint the session runs on; mediaAccess is NONE until the server authorizes the session's media (initiator, or the participant's single winning device), REVOKED for ever after removal; mediaAdmittedAt is when the provider confirmed an admitted connection; removedAt is set when the session was removed.

calling.ErrorCode.description: Stable public error codes of the Calling service.

calling.ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response body. Messages are fixed, safe strings; authentication failures are uniform.

calling.HistoryDestinationType.description: Enterprise destinations a listing may be narrowed to.

calling.HistoryDirection.description: Direction of a Call relative to the principal whose history it is.

calling.ParticipantOutcome.description: The outcome of a Call for ONE logical participant, derived from Call evidence only (participant, ring offers on every device, session connection intervals, the Call's state) — never from a push, a realtime signal or a client acknowledgement, and never stored as a flag. OUTBOUND: ANSWERED, NOT_ANSWERED (ended unanswered), IN_PROGRESS. INBOUND, first match wins: ANSWERED (an offer accepted on any of the participant's devices, or a session connected), DECLINED, ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE (the offers were won by another participant of the same answer group — a ring-group or queue colleague), RINGING (an offer is live), MISSED (offered on at least one device and every offer ended unanswered), NOT_REACHED (never offered, Call over), IN_PROGRESS. A losing device of a participant that answered is never a second (missed) entry.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallCore.description: Fields of every Call representation (HTTP API, call-control results). Provider-independent: no provider or carrier identifiers, execution bindings, media identities, telephone numbers or protected contact data.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version: 1 at creation, +1 per state transition.

endedAt.description: When the call reached a terminal state.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallEndpointKi.description: Neutral kind of a registered application endpoint (a device / client instance of a principal).

calling.calling.common.v1.CallEndpointPr.description: Presence hint used to order ringing; never an authorization.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallFailureCat.description: Normalized failure category. Provider error codes never become categories.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallInvitation.description: Why a ring offer exists: the Call itself, or an application transfer to a new target.
State of a ring offer to one endpoint. PENDING and RINGING are live; every other state is terminal and final (an offer is never revived). The server owns expiry.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallKind.description: Neutral media kind of a Call. No consumer business meaning.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallMediaAcces.description: A session's media authority: NONE until the server authorizes it (initiator, or the single winning device of a participant), AUTHORIZED while it may hold media credentials, REVOKED for ever after removal or the end of the session.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallMediaCapab.description: Media capabilities the server authorizes for one session's media connection. Derived from server state (call kind, participant permissions, hold); never chosen by the client. There is no administrative, recording, room-creation or room-listing capability.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallState.description: Canonical business state of a Call. Terminal: ENDED, DECLINED, BUSY, NO_ANSWER, FAILED, CANCELLED.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallSummary.description: A call as listed and as returned by call-control commands.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallTerminalRe.description: How a Call reached its terminal state. ENDED records its completion evidence; every other terminal state has the reason of the same name.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallTransferFa.description: Why a transfer did not complete. A failed transfer returns the Call to its pre-transfer state when the remaining parties still have a media path.

calling.calling.common.v1.CallTransferSt.description: Application transfer lifecycle, kept out of the Call state (the Call is TRANSFERRING while a transfer is active).

calling.calling.common.v1.SafeEventData.description: Bounded, flat, privacy-safe event data: at most 32 snake_case keys that never name secrets, credentials, contact data or provider / carrier identifiers; values are booleans, numbers, safe text or short lists of safe text.

calling.calling.common.v1.SafeText.description: Bounded text without control characters that never looks like a telephone number (+<digit>) or a tel: / sip: URI.

calling.calling.control.v1.AcceptResult.description: The offer was accepted: this endpoint's device won its participant's answer (single winner), the participant's other offers became ANSWERED_ELSEWHERE, and sessionId is the winning session that may now request media credentials. callAnswered is true when this acceptance moved the Call to ANSWERED.

reason.description: Why the action is unavailable: the credential lacks calls.write, the Call's state does not allow it, or the configured media provider cannot enforce it.

calling.calling.control.v1.AvailableActi.description: Server-derived actions currently valid for a Call and the authenticated credential. The client never computes them from local state.

calling.calling.control.v1.CallInvitatio.description: A ring offer of a Call to one endpoint of one target participant. Status and terminal reason always agree: an offer that expired, was cancelled or was answered elsewhere can never be accepted, and a live offer has neither.

calling.calling.control.v1.CallTransfer.description: An application transfer of a Call (kept out of the Call state).

calling.calling.control.v1.CommandReques.description: Body of cancel, end, hold, resume and session removal: the expected Call version and nothing else (no state, reason or permission can be sent).

expectedVersion.description: The Call version the command was decided on (optimistic concurrency). A different current version is refused with 409 STALE_CALL_VERSION.

calling.calling.control.v1.ControlResult.description: Result of cancel, end, hold and resume: the Call after the command. END answers with ENDING until provider cleanup is confirmed, or ENDED once it is.

calling.calling.control.v1.CreateCallReq.description: Body of POST /v1/calls. The initiator calls from one of its registered ACTIVE endpoints; every target is a principal of the same application environment (resolved inside the credential's scope; an unknown or foreign principal is 404). One target is a one-to-one call, several targets a group call (at most the configured participant limit, 16 by default, including the initiator). The server decides authorization, routing, ringing and media; nothing of that can be sent. Part E: instead of principal targets, ONE protected public-network contact (targetContactReference, an opaque ContactReference issued by Privacy Relay — never a telephone number) under a Privacy Relay Session: an APP_TO_PSTN call executed by Telephony after Privacy Relay (PUBLIC_RELAY), the Routing Engine, the telecom switches and a durable spend reservation all allow it (403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED / 503 PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE / 429 TELECOM_SPEND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED otherwise). The caller identity is selected server-side; no request field can set it. Part E §47 callback relay: callbackRequested with the requester's own verified protected contact (initiatorContactReference) and the callee's (targetContactReference) under a Privacy Relay Session, without an endpoint: Telephony calls the requester first and the callee only after the first leg answered; both legs are bridged in one Call (two legs, two usage facts).

initiatorEndpointId.description: The initiator's registered ACTIVE endpoint. Required for application and APP_TO_PSTN calls; absent for a callback relay.

callbackRequested.description: The requester asks to be called back on its own protected contact and bridged to the callee (Part E §47). A request, not a route: Privacy Relay and the Routing Engine decide whether CALLBACK_RELAY is allowed (403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED otherwise).

initiatorContactReference.description: The requester's own verified protected contact (callback relay only).

targetContactReference.description: A protected contact (opaque ContactReference). Requires privacyRelaySessionId; exclusive with targetPrincipalIds.

privacyRelaySessionId.description: Optional Privacy Relay Session (cfmeet.privacy-relay.session). The call becomes a PROTECTED call: Calling asks Privacy Relay for current authority (PRIVACY_RELAY_V1) before anything rings, records the decision and fails closed (503 PRIVACY_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE) when no answer can be obtained; it never falls back to APP_DIRECT_V1. VOICE only. A transfer of a protected call re-authorizes the new target.

targetExtension.description: Part F: an enterprise extension number (an internal short code, never a telephone number) resolved in the credential's scope and routed by enterprise configuration over ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL (no public leg, no spend). Requires enterprise.calls.use and initiatorEndpointId; excludes every other target. An unknown number is 404; a policy refusal 403 CALL_NOT_AUTHORIZED; enterprise calling disabled 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.

presentedNumberResourceId.description: Part IV L: a Digital Communications Number (CF Meet Number Resource id — never a telephone number) to present as the caller identity of a targetContactReference call instead of the session's relay identity. Numbering must hold it ACTIVE for the credential's scope with usable outbound voice, and the initiator must be entitled to present it: the owner of a personal / professional number, or an ACTIVE enterprise principal reached through an organization number's voice target (organizational scope alone never suffices). 403 PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED otherwise; 503 PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE while Numbering is unreachable. No other identity is ever substituted.

calling.calling.control.v1.CreateCallRes.description: Response of POST /v1/calls (201; replays return the same body with Idempotent-Replayed: true). The call is normally RINGING with one live offer per eligible target endpoint; it can still be ROUTING while the media resource is being prepared (the reconciler resumes it), or already FAILED (ROUTING when no target has an eligible endpoint, MEDIA when the resource could not be prepared in time). Part F: an enterprise Call (targetExtension) additionally carries its enterprise context; while it waits in a queue or IVR it may list only the initiator.

enterprise.description: Present for an enterprise Call only: its safe enterprise context.

calling.calling.control.v1.DeclineResult.description: The offer was declined. Only this endpoint's offer ends; the Call ends as DECLINED only when every live offer of every pending target has been declined.

calling.calling.control.v1.EmptyRequest.description: A command without parameters (media credentials): an empty object or no body. The server derives every capability; any field is refused.

calling.calling.control.v1.Endpoint.description: A registered application endpoint of a principal. Presence is a routing hint only.

endpointKey.description: Opaque client-chosen device key, unique per principal while ACTIVE. Never a telephone number or a tel: / sip: URI.

calling.calling.control.v1.EndpointCapab.description: Media the endpoint can handle. Every application call needs audio: endpoints without audio are never rung; an audio-only endpoint is rung for VIDEO calls too and simply publishes no camera.

calling.calling.control.v1.InvitationCom.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/accept|decline (backend answering on behalf of one of the target's endpoints).

expectedVersion.description: The Call version the command was decided on (optimistic concurrency). A different current version is refused with 409 STALE_CALL_VERSION.

calling.calling.control.v1.MediaCredenti.description: A short-lived join credential for one authorized session's connection to the Call's media resource: the connection URL, the opaque token, its expiry and the capabilities the connection receives once admitted. Room names, provider identifiers, provider keys and administrative grants are never part of it. A losing device, a removed session, an expired offer or a terminal Call never receives one.

url.description: Calling's media connection gateway URL (wss:// in production), never the media server itself.

token.description: Opaque join credential bound to this session's media identity, its current media generation and the Call's media resource, sealed by Calling's media edge: the media server does not accept it directly, and the gateway admits it only while that generation of the session holds media access. It carries no administrative grant.

calling.calling.control.v1.RecoveredInvi.description: An offer of the endpoint as recovered after a reconnect, with the authoritative Call state. actionable is true only for a RINGING, unexpired offer of a Call that can still be answered.
Response of GET /v1/calling/invitations (signaling credential): the endpoint's live and recently finished offers.

calling.calling.control.v1.RegisterEndpo.description: Body of POST /v1/calling/endpoints. Registering the same key for the same principal again refreshes it (200).

endpointKey.description: Opaque client-chosen device key, unique per principal while ACTIVE. Never a telephone number or a tel: / sip: URI.

oneOf.description: Opaque reference to a push target held by the application (no push token).

calling.calling.control.v1.SessionRemova.description: Result of removing one session: its media access is revoked and the provider connection removed (or queued for enforcement).

calling.calling.control.v1.SignalingCred.description: A short-lived Call Signaling Credential for one endpoint, handed to the device by the application backend.
